# Fabric campaign (E2)

Warden on a real codebase: Fabric ERP (FastAPI + SQLAlchemy 2 + Postgres RLS, double-entry
ledger, Indian GST). Each issue runs plan → fix → verify → draft PR; issues are grouped into
waves by the files their plans touch, each wave's passing fixes are merged with
`git merge --no-ff` into one integration image in the sandbox, and the full gate runs on it.

## Notes (2026-10-15, written by hand; the tables above are generated)

**Question: is Warden useful on a real industrial codebase?** On this run, not yet as an
autonomous fixer. Its safety side held up. 1 of 9 issues was fixed and verified (#196, draft
[Fabric-Inventory#226](https://github.com/moiz-lakkadkutta/Fabric-Inventory/pull/226): Fabric's
own CI ran 7/7 jobs green). The other 8 FAILed, and no FAIL produced a branch or a PR. Total spend
was **$4.81** for 15 attempts on 9 issues (mean $0.32 per attempt), with a per-issue cap of $1.50.

### What was run

- **Fabric's open backlog is thin.** When the campaign started, 4 issues were open. #215 and #216
  are already fixed on `main` and wait for a CA sign-off. #217 *is* the CA sign-off, so it has no
  code. That leaves **#210** (test only) as the one open code issue, run at the live head
  (`aaf85a9`). The base image was built at `8cfc493`, 82 commits behind. The head reached the
  sandbox as a git bundle (no network, no token), then `alembic upgrade head` ran on both DBs:
  50 s. The full gate on that base was green: **2243 passed** in 1107 s, mypy, ruff, one alembic
  head, no OpenAPI drift.
- **Every other issue is a closed one, replayed** at the commit before its human fix. Warden got
  the issue text only, with comments hidden. These are the six issues of PR #212 (#196 #197 #200
  #205 #206 #207 at `43f3851^`), #215 at `60ae34b^`, and #216 at `3eee35f^`. A replay is the only
  way to grade a result against what a human actually shipped.
- **Hunter issues.** None carried `warden-hunt` when the campaign started. Two appeared while it
  ran, #225 and #227: historical cross-firm IDOR replays at `d9c37cb^`. The Hunter session ran
  them itself through `warden run` (see each issue's closing comment), so they are **not** rows
  in this CSV. Both were confirmed by the Hunter (reproduced twice) and both were FAIL with no PR:
  #225 took 4 runs for $1.49, #227 a best-of-2 for $0.52. On #225 the repro failed on the base
  as required and stayed red with every candidate's change, so the verifier rejected security
  fixes that did not work. On #227 the chosen candidate had a valid repro, but it never finished
  and left one suite failure.
- **Two configs.** A = 40 tool turns, 1 candidate (`camp-head-1`, `camp-replay-212`). B = 60 turns,
  best-of-2 (`camp-head-2`, `camp-replay-212-b` re-ran A's five FAILs, then `camp-replay-215`,
  `camp-replay-216`). B cost about 2.5× A per issue and fixed nothing more.

### Why 8 of 9 failed: the implementer, not the pipeline

- **Only 2 of 15 chosen candidates called `finish`.** One was #196, the PASS. The other was #207
  in config B: it finished after 11 turns with no test, and the spec review found 3 of 4 stated
  behaviours missing. Every other attempt used all its turns.
- **Fabric's test files are large** (`test_manufacturing_masters.py` 916 lines,
  `test_migrations_router.py` 926). Nemotron 3 Super loops on them:
  - It re-reads the same range after being told it already has it. Warden's "unchanged since
    turn N" reply fired 30, 71 and 86 times in single runs (#200 A, #197 B, #200 B).
  - It re-sends a whole file through `write_file`. On #210 (A), 7 of 40 replies hit the
    8192-token completion limit, and the call arrived with no `content` (FEEDBACK.md). Warden now
    says why (`54747c7`); in config B, #210 got further, then wrote a test that does not collect.
- **When it did write tests, the theater check usually threw them out, correctly.** Across six
  attempts, eight new tests failed on the unfixed base for the wrong reason (AttributeError,
  ModuleNotFoundError, collection error) or stayed red with the fix. None was counted as a repro.

### What the verifier got right

- **No false PASS that we know of.** The one PASS is a fix Fabric's CI accepts, with a repro that
  fails on the base (`camp-replay-212-196`). It is the same issue Warden solved in #221: the
  issue it can solve, solved again, for $0.11.
- **#207 (B) shows why the spec review exists.** The suite was green (1506 passed) and mypy and
  ruff were clean, but the candidate implemented 1 of 4 stated behaviours. A test-and-lint gate
  alone would have passed it.
- **#215 was a near miss, rejected for the right reasons.** Its repro failed on the base for the
  right reason and the suite was green (1833 passed). But mypy was red, one of the issue's two
  behaviours (a 422 from `create_draft_invoice`) was missing, and the implementer never finished.
- **PENDING-HUMAN was set on 13 of 15 rows** (money, schema, tax, security), which is what an ERP
  ledger needs. One miss: the planner did not tag #215 (a GST rule) as `tax`. It got the label
  anyway through `schema` / `security` / `money`.

### Waves and merging (D2)

- **In the campaigns, no wave had more than one passing candidate**, so each wave merged at most
  one patch. Wave 1 of `camp-replay-212` merged #196 onto the integration image, and the gate on
  it was green (1507 passed, mypy, ruff, alembic, OpenAPI). The integration branch was pushed as
  `warden/campaign-camp-replay-212-w1`. Waves 2 and 3 forked that image, and their PRs would have
  stacked on that branch.
- **Mechanics check on real patches** (no model calls, no PR; `merge-live.json`). Four real
  Fabric candidates (#196, #197, #205, #206) were merged onto one base with `git merge --no-ff`:
  4 kept runs, a fork chain, **no conflicts**. The gate on the integrated image then went red
  (suite 1506 passed / **6 failed**, mypy ✗, ruff ✗). That is expected, since three of the four
  were FAIL candidates, and it is why the merged image gets its own gate: a clean merge says
  nothing about the result.

### Limits of this campaign

- 9 issues, one run per config. Per-issue outcomes swing with sampling (see SWE-rebench pilots
  1–3), so treat these as a sample, not a rate.
- Replays run on an image whose DB is migrated at `8cfc493`, which is newer than `43f3851^`.
  #227's write-up flags one test that fails on the unfixed base for this reason.
- A test-only issue (#210) does not fit Warden's verifier. The theater check wants a new test
  that *fails* on the unfixed code, and a coverage test for correct behaviour passes there.
- Wall clock: about 15 min per issue in config A and about 30 min in B. Up to 4 issues ran in
  parallel (`WARDEN_MAX_FORKS=4`). The Fabric gate alone takes about 18 min at head.

## Re-run after the implementer fixes: `camp-replay-212-c` and `-d` (2026-10-15, by hand)

The same six #212 issues at `43f3851^` in config A (40 turns, 1 candidate), cap $0.80/issue,
after the B3 implementer changes (docs/status.md §1l). `-c` ran with the first three changes: 200-line
read pages, the large-file write refusal and auto-finish. `-d` also ran with edit mode, which
withholds the read tools after an escalated re-read or a second idle nudge.

| metric (6 issues, from events.jsonl) | `camp-replay-212` (before) | `-c` | `-d` |
|---|---|---|---|
| PASS | **1** (#196) | 0 | 0 |
| valid repro (theater) | 1 | 0 | **2** (#196, #206) |
| `finish` called / auto-finished | 1 / — | 0 / 0 | 1 / 0 |
| runs that edited a source file | 1 | 0 | **5** |
| `replace_in_file` calls / `write_file` | 3 / 4 | 0 / 2 | **26** / 7 |
| cached re-read answers | 71 | 87 | **32** |
| replies cut at 8192 tokens | 2 | 0 | 0 |
| tool turns (sum) | 226 | 240 | 238 |
| USD | $1.11 | $1.14 | $1.35 |

- **The loop is broken. The fix rate did not move.** In `-d` five of six candidates edited
  source code, and every one added tests. Before, one did. Edit mode fired 12 times, and a
  read sent anyway was refused instead of served. Two repros were valid, against one before.
  No candidate PASSed:
  - #196 called `finish` itself with a correct repro and 1 of 1 stated behaviour implemented, but
    left 2 suite failures and mypy red.
  - #206 had a valid repro and green new tests. Auto-finish declined it twice (a `ruff` error
    that autofix can't fix), and it left 2 suite failures.
  - #197, #200, #205 and #207 wrote repros that fail for the wrong reason (TypeError,
    ImportError, collection error) or stay red with the fix.
- **Auto-finish never fired, and declined 5 times, correctly each time**: the new tests were red
  (#200, #207), did not collect (#205), or lint was red (#206 ×2). It is a no-op on these
  issues, not a false PASS source.
- **`-c` alone was worse than before.** Without edit mode the STOP note did not change Super's
  behaviour: 16 cached answers for a 50-line test file on #196, 23 on #207, no source edit
  in any run. #196 PASSed in `camp-replay-212` and FAILed in `-c` and `-d`. One sample per issue
  is noise-dominated (see SWE-rebench pilots 1–3).
- **The large-file write refusal fired 3 times** (write_file on an existing >300-line file).
  No reply hit the 8192 cap in `-c` or `-d`: the implementer now sends max_tokens=16384.
- No PR was opened: a FAIL opens nothing.
